capabilities.need: Ask the user questions in rounds
capabilities.via: ask_user shows question cards (1 to 4 questions, 2 to 4 options each, one answer per question)
the user picks the project folder with the folder button; bash and the file tools work in it

capabilities.need: Show a file (reel, lab, cards, MP4)
capabilities.via: show_page opens an HTML or video file of the project or the skill in the preview pane

capabilities.need: Fill in the project questions and decide on assets on screens
capabilities.via: the project settings panel (a button in the top bar: audience, message, tone, languages, formats, duration, constraints, control level) and the Resources tab of the Library, in the editing workspace; a new project first asks for its base configuration (conversation and reel languages, formats, target duration and a look), as one question per screen in a wizard (Beginner mode) or as one compact form (Expert mode), and the workspace opens when it is complete (an existing project is never blocked: the checks say what is missing); the guided path ends in the workspace; update_parameter and update_asset change them as plain cards the user accepts or refuses

the project settings panel (Look is a list of six rows, each opening its editor with a back button; while it is open the viewer shows the project's design system as a read-only board, and each editor pins the current choice as a large card above the other options: the looks board, a palette editor with a contrast check, fonts with licence warnings, the default background and its mood, motion moods and the effects pack, each previewed by the same engine as the reel); the catalogues are picked where they are used, with the engine's previews (a background in a scene's Look tab, an animation on an item or in the scene's Effects tab, a scene transition in the transition inspector, the six preview-only transitions shown but never chosen) and an optional floating Catalogue (looks, palettes, backgrounds, effects, transitions) to drag onto a scene, an item or a marker; update_decision changes the global look as plain cards the user accepts or refuses; a global change that would redraw locked scenes inheriting it (not those with their own look) lists them on the card, with the choice to apply anyway or refuse, for the user's own edits as for Clap's

capabilities.need: Write the storyboard, review each scene and give the go on screens
capabilities.via: the Scenes tab of the Library (the scene library: create, edit, duplicate, archive, rename (a name beside the stable ID, edited in place); every list reorders by dragging a handle, with a gap that opens; each scene opens into a tree of Composition (every element in priority order: words, images and sounds, a linked resource always being one), Effects and Look (background, palette, fonts, each inherited or replaced, with a badge on a scene that replaces something), a click on a group or a node opening the matching inspector tab on that element), the Storyboard strip at the bottom, a storyboard that is an editing timeline (dark, filling its panel: it opens with the whole film in the width, the frames and their thumbnails at the height of the lane, a ruler in seconds and bars, the music directly under the frames with a filled waveform or a place to drop an audio file; zoom with minus and plus, pinch, Command-Plus, Command-Minus, Command-0 and Fit selection, anchored on the pointer or the playhead, the scale remembered per project; each frame shows its ID, its name when there is room and its duration; transition markers are diamonds on the cuts; a toolbar with the transport, the snap level, ripple, Add scene and the one primary action Validate then Give the Go; space plays, the arrows go from scene to scene; frames drag to reorder, edges stretch, and the grid levels are beat, bar, section, drop or off), and native reading-budget, feasibility and music checks, which the Checks tab of the left panel groups by area (Project, Resources, Scenes, Storyboard, Music, Build) with a count of what is red or orange, a click opening the element concerned) and the Inspector (tabs Settings, Composition, Effects and Look; Composition is the ordered list of what the scene contains, each element with its words or resource, colour, animation and instruction, each attribute fixed or auto, at a control level of auto, guided or precise; a scene's Look is locked to the project's until a switch per group replaces it for that scene only, and a dropped background, palette or look asks "Replace for this scene only?" first; review: OK (Validated), MODIFY (WIP with a note) or DITCH, plus a lock switch (a Locked scene refuses any change to its content, duration or look, with a reason; its place in the montage still moves; lock_scene for Clap, one card); the Go button that only the user can press); add_scene, update_scene, enable_scene, move_scene, set_scene_override and add_, update_, remove_ and move_content_item, set_scene_duration, set_transition, set_track and set_grid propose changes as plain cards the user accepts or refuses

capabilities.need: Build the reel, test it and play it
capabilities.via: the Build and preview view of the workspace: after the Go, the app writes vN/film.json (the montage: starts, durations, transitions) and you write the rest of the vN folder (project.json and a main.js in the film format: one module per scene and one SRF.fromData call); the app runs build.py, harness.js and smoke_player.js, shows each result in green or red, and plays vN/dist/index.html in the viewer at the playhead of the reel, with the music; outputs stay in the project folder

capabilities.need: Let the user read and edit the project files next to the assistant
capabilities.via: an Advanced panel (off by default) shows the project's files with editors and a per-file history; propose_edit offers a change to a file as a diff the user accepts or refuses; get_state reads the project's state

capabilities.need: Remember what was decided between sessions
capabilities.via: a project memory (.studio/memory.json: decisions with their reasons, preferences, rejected options, constraints, open questions, facts) that you write with remember, update_memory and forget and that the user reads, edits and deletes in the What Clap knows view; an append-only journal of every typed operation, refusals, undos and redos included; and a short summary of each session. At the start of a session the app gives you the memory, what the user refused and the last summaries as data, not as instructions; get_state is still the truth about the project. The History tab of the project settings shows the sessions and the journal; the brief's Decisions log and Assumptions sections come from them
screenshot_preview captures the preview pane (a page, a contact sheet or the reel, after show_page) as an image the model can look at

capabilities.fallback: no hosted pages: deliver the HTML file and say how to share it

capabilities.need: Assemble the reel from its scene files
capabilities.via: the build runs scripts/assemble.py (through build.py) on the version folder: film.json, one scenes/<ID>.js per scene and reel.js become main.js without any AI, deterministically; a scene without a usable file is a visible placeholder listed in assembly.json; Clap's generate_scenes tool writes the file of one or several scenes only (a card to confirm, never a locked scene), and .studio/build.json records what each scene file was generated from, so a scene is not generated, up to date or stale (not shown in the interface yet)
bash runs in a login shell in the project folder
numpy and ffmpeg when the owner ran the environment setup; the environment check reports what is missing

capabilities.fallback: no web search: ask the user for facts and documents; never invent figures
